questions.coherence: One design. Format owns the pure parts of each import or save: the up-front ZIP listing; the draw.io XML caps and own-key lookups; font inventory, plan, job runner, the candidate and its record shape behind injected WebAssembly and timers; and the pack encoder's single-pass grouping. Hosts own workers, timers and fs. The studio and the CLI run the same subset code over the same pinned modules, each with its own reopen check (reopensWithSubsets and reopensIntact are near-duplicates, which is tolerable). The studio importer reuses registerSvgLibrary and FileBar.shapePackSources, so imported packs save the way M18.192 packs do. The witness cleanup changes stay inside CleanupCoordinator.

findings.evidence: subsetFontGaps (and coveredBy, line 126) parse a file's font.subset.unicodes with no bound on length or pair count. They then test each codepoint with pairs.some(...), which is O(codepoints x pairs). apps/studio/src/file-session.ts:303 calls gapsOf(document) on every successful save, whether or not subsetting is on. font.subset arrives from any opened .flux, because asset records are loose (ADR-0201). Measured with tsx: a 1.6 MB unicodes string (200k single-codepoint parts) against 5000 CJK codepoints takes 13.8 s in subsetFontGaps.
findings.failure_scenario: A crafted .flux whose font record carries a multi-megabyte font.subset.unicodes, together with text that uses a few thousand distinct characters, freezes the studio's main thread for tens of seconds or longer on every Save. With subsetting on, the same cost hits coveredBy, both in the studio and in convert --subset-fonts. The cost grows with file size rather than with the 5 MiB font caps.

findings.evidence: leg('CLI pack import and font-subset option exercise real files', () => tests('packages/cli/src/pack-import.test.ts')): that suite has no --subset-fonts case (grep finds only pack-import cases). findings.failure_scenario: A regression that breaks convert --subset-fonts, or its result.fonts --json contract, leaves the completion gate green under a leg that claims to cover it. Ordinary CI would still run the e2e, but the completion gate's claim is false.

findings.failure_scenario: The calibration ratio for a hashing- and JSON-heavy encode is not machine-invariant against the layout calibration workload. If hosted units exceed 36.07 (+15 %), the nightly perf job goes red on unchanged code, and someone re-records under pressure. If they come in well below, the regression budget is loose by that margin with nobody noticing.
